title: Academic Calendar and Exam Regulations
summary: Comprehensive guide to course registration deadlines, add/drop periods, official grading scale, exam deferral procedures, and medical excuse policies.

sections.heading: 1. Key Academic Dates (Academic Year 2026-2027)
lines: Fall Semester Registration Deadline: September 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST.
Add/Drop Period: August 28 - September 11, 2026 (100% tuition adjustment, no transcript mark).
Course Withdrawal Deadline (W grade recorded): October 23, 2026.
Final Examination Week: December 14 - December 21, 2026 (Room assignments posted in Student Portal).

sections.heading: 2. Official Grading Scale & GPA Computation
lines: Dean's Honor List requirement: Term GPA >= 3.75 with minimum 15 graded credits and zero Incompletes.
Academic Probation occurs if cumulative GPA drops below 2.00.

sections.heading: 3. Exam Deferral & Medical Absence Protocol
lines: Students with documented medical emergencies must submit Form MED-9 within 48 hours of missed exam.
Documentation must be signed by a licensed practitioner and verified by Student Health Clinic (Room 102).
Approved deferred examinations are scheduled during the first two weeks of the subsequent semester.
A temporary grade of 'I' (Incomplete) expires into 'F' after 60 calendar days if unresolved.

sections.heading: 4. Departmental Contact Information
lines: Registrar Office: Hall of Administration, Room 114 | registrar@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-2831
Walk-in Hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 4:30 PM EST.

title: Tuition Refunds and Financial Aid Policy
summary: Tuition billing schedules, payment installment plans, prorated refund percentages, merit scholarship maintenance conditions, and FAFSA compliance rules.

sections.heading: 1. Tuition Due Dates & Installment Plans
lines: Fall 2026 Tuition Due Date: August 18, 2026. Spring 2027 Due Date: January 12, 2027.
Late Payment Fee: $125 assessed on accounts with outstanding balances after payment due date.
Deferred 4-Pay Installment Plan: $45 non-refundable enrollment fee; payments split across 4 monthly dates (Aug 18, Sep 18, Oct 18, Nov 18).

sections.heading: 2. Prorated Tuition Refund Schedule
lines: Withdrawal during Weeks 1-2 (before Sep 11, 2026): 100% tuition refund (minus $100 processing fee).
Withdrawal during Week 3 (Sep 12 - Sep 18, 2026): 75% tuition refund.
Withdrawal during Week 4 (Sep 19 - Sep 25, 2026): 50% tuition refund.
Withdrawal after Week 4 (Sep 26 onward): 0% refund. Lab fees and technology fees are strictly non-refundable.

sections.heading: 3. Merit Scholarships & Financial Aid Renewal
lines: Horizon Presidential Merit Scholarship ($12,000/yr) requires cumulative GPA >= 3.50 and 30 credits/yr.
Dean's Excellence Grant ($6,000/yr) requires cumulative GPA >= 3.20.
Scholarship appeals must be filed via Form FA-APPEAL before July 15 for the upcoming academic year.

sections.heading: 4. Departmental Contact Information
lines: Bursar Office: Financial Services Tower, Suite 210 | bursar@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-4420
Financial Aid Helpdesk: finaid@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-4421

title: Campus Housing and Residence Handbook
summary: Residence hall living regulations, mandatory quiet hours, overnight guest registration rules, facility maintenance turnaround SLAs, and checkout inspection charges.

sections.heading: 1. Residence Quiet Hours & Community Standards
lines: Standard Quiet Hours: Sunday-Thursday 10:00 PM - 8:00 AM; Friday-Saturday 12:00 Midnight - 9:00 AM.
24-Hour Courtesy Hours are continuously in effect campus-wide across all residential buildings.
Exam Week Quiet Hours: Strict 24-hour quiet period begins 48 hours prior to the first final examination.
First noise violation: Written warning. Second violation: $75 community fine. Third: Housing review.

sections.heading: 2. Overnight Guest Policies & Sign-In Requirements
lines: All non-resident guests must register at the hall front desk with a valid government or student ID.
No guest may stay more than 3 consecutive nights or more than 6 nights total in a single calendar month.
Roommate written consent via the Residential Life Portal is required prior to host guest arrival.

sections.heading: 3. Maintenance Requests & Room Checkout Inspections
lines: Emergency repairs (water leaks, power loss, door lock failure): Dispatched within 2 hours (24/7 hotline).
Routine maintenance (lighting, furniture adjustment): Resolved within 3 to 5 business days.
Move-out inspection fee schedule: Uncleaned room fee $150; lost key replacement $65; wall drywall repair $85.

sections.heading: 4. Housing Contact Information
lines: Residential Life Office: Horizon Village Center, Room B12 | reslife@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-3300
24/7 On-Call Resident Assistant Dispatch: (555) 019-3399

title: IT Services, WiFi, and Software Licensing
summary: Campus-wide Eduroam wireless connection guidelines, student VPN configuration, complimentary software licensing (JetBrains, Office 365, MATLAB), and identity security protocols.

sections.heading: 1. Eduroam Wireless Network Configuration
lines: SSID: 'eduroam' (WPA2/WPA3 Enterprise authentication).
Username format: studentID@horizon.edu (e.g., 20268841@horizon.edu). Use your Horizon Portal password.
Guest Wi-Fi network: 'Horizon-Guest' provides 4Mbps bandwidth throttled connection, valid for 24 hours.
IoT Devices (consoles, smart TVs) must be registered via mac-auth.horizon.edu using device MAC address.

sections.heading: 2. Free Student Software Licenses & Developer Tools
lines: Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams (install on up to 5 personal devices).
JetBrains All Products Pack: Free educational license renewed annually with university email domain.
MATLAB & Simulink Campus-Wide Suite: Download installer from mathworks.com/license/horizon.
GitHub Student Developer Pack: Access via github.com/education using university single sign-on.

sections.heading: 3. Campus VPN & Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
lines: GlobalProtect VPN endpoint: vpn.horizon.edu (required to access research clusters and library proxies off-campus).
MFA authentication is mandatory for all accounts via Duo Security or Google Authenticator.
Password self-service reset portal: identity.horizon.edu (passwords expire every 180 days).

sections.heading: 4. IT Helpdesk Contacts
lines: IT Support Center: Tech Commons Ground Floor, Room 045 | itsupport@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-4357 (HELP)
Hours: Monday-Thursday 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM, Friday 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM EST.

title: Library and Research Facilities Policy
summary: Circulation borrowing limits, interlibrary loan guidelines, overdue item fee structures, 24/7 collaborative study room booking procedures, and high-performance computing room access.

sections.heading: 1. Book & Equipment Borrowing Limits
lines: Undergraduate students may borrow up to 25 physical books simultaneously for a 28-day loan cycle.
Course reserve textbooks: 3-hour in-library checkout only, renewable once if no hold queue exists.
Multimedia equipment checkout (laptops, DSLR cameras, podcast audio kits): 72-hour checkout limit.
Interlibrary Loans (ILLiad): Free of charge; electronic articles delivered within 48 hours.

sections.heading: 2. Overdue Fines & Lost Material Charges
lines: Standard circulation books: $0.50 per day per item (maximum fine cap $25.00 per item).
Course reserve materials: $2.00 per hour overdue fee (no fine cap).
Tech equipment: $15.00 per day overdue fee. Items 14 days overdue are declared lost ($850 replacement invoice).
Fine waivers: Allowed once per academic year for first-time minor infractions (under $10) via Front Desk appeal.

sections.heading: 3. 24/7 Study Room Reservations & Research Labs
lines: Group study rooms (Rooms 201-224): Reserve online via library.horizon.edu/rooms up to 7 days in advance.
Booking duration: Maximum 3 hours per student per day; room reservations forfeit after 15 minutes no-show.
Level 4 is designated as a Permanent Silent Study Zone. Cell phone calls are strictly prohibited on Levels 3 and 4.

sections.heading: 4. Library Contact Information
lines: Main Library: Founders Library Building | library@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-2100
Research Librarian Desk: Chat online at library.horizon.edu/chat (Mon-Fri 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM).

title: Student Conduct and Academic Integrity Code
department: Office of Student Conduct & Community Standards
summary: Definitions of academic dishonesty, strict guidelines on generative AI usage across coursework, disciplinary sanction tiers, and the formal judicial appeal tribunal process.

sections.heading: 1. Violations of Academic Integrity
lines: Plagiarism: Submitting work prepared by another, failing to cite quotations, paraphrasing without attribution.
Unauthorized Collaboration: Sharing assignment solutions or exam answers without explicit instructor consent.
Falsification: Fabricating research experimental data, forging academic or medical certificates.
Contract Cheating: Purchasing essays or code from commercial essay mills or freelance third parties.

sections.heading: 2. Generative AI Tools Usage Policy
lines: Category Green (Permitted): Use of AI for grammar checking, brainstorming, and literature discovery when cited.
Category Yellow (Conditional): AI code assistance permitted only when explicitly designated in course syllabus.
Category Red (Prohibited): Submitting unedited AI-generated prose or code as original student submissions.
All AI assistance must be disclosed in an 'AI Acknowledgement Statement' accompanying the assignment.

sections.heading: 3. Sanction Tiers & Disciplinary Tribunal Appeals
lines: Level 1 Violation: Reprimand, mandatory 0 on the affected assignment, mandatory Ethics Workshop completion.
Level 2 Violation: 'XF' grade (Failure due to Academic Dishonesty) recorded on transcript for the entire course.
Level 3 Violation (Repeated offense): Formal recommendation for one-year academic suspension or expulsion.
Appeals: Must be submitted to the Academic Integrity Tribunal within 5 business days of sanction notice.

sections.heading: 4. Conduct Office Contact
lines: Office of Student Conduct: Union Hall, Room 308 | conduct@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-5500
Confidential Integrity Hotline: (555) 019-SAFE

title: Campus Health, Wellness, and Counseling Services
summary: Outpatient primary medical care hours, mental health therapy session allowances, mandatory immunization deadlines, student health insurance waivers, and crisis hotlines.

sections.heading: 1. Medical Clinic Services & Hours
lines: Primary Care Clinic: Wellness Center Level 1 | Open Mon-Fri 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM; Sat 9:00 AM - 1:00 PM.
Co-pay: $0 co-pay for full-time enrolled students for basic physician consultations and nurse triage.
In-house services: Rapid strep/flu testing ($15), routine bloodwork, travel immunizations, minor sutures.
After-hours nurse triage helpline: (555) 019-WELL (available 24 hours/day, 365 days/year).

sections.heading: 2. Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS)
lines: Enrolled students receive up to 10 free individual counseling sessions per academic year.
Unlimited access to specialized group therapy workshops (Anxiety Management, Graduate Stress, Mindfulness).
Urgent crisis walk-in appointments available daily with no prior booking between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM.
Emergency Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Dial 988 or text 'HORIZON' to 741741.

sections.heading: 3. Immunization Requirements & Insurance Waivers
lines: Mandatory Vaccines: MMR (2 doses), Meningococcal ACWY (within 5 years for dorm residents), Tdap (within 10 yrs).
Immunization documentation due date: August 1 for Fall semester enrollment (holds placed if incomplete).
Student Health Insurance Plan ($1,850/yr) is billed automatically unless an approved waiver is filed by Sep 1.

sections.heading: 4. Wellness Contacts
lines: Appointments: healthcenter@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-9355 | Portal: patient.horizon.edu
Counseling Desk: caps@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-9356

title: Career Services, Internships, and Co-Op Guide
summary: Undergraduate internship academic credit qualification, Handshake job portal access, on-campus career fairs schedule, resume review clinics, and international student CPT/OPT protocols.

sections.heading: 1. Internship for Academic Credit Requirements
lines: Students must have completed at least 45 cumulative credit hours with a minimum GPA of 2.75.
Every 45 verified workplace hours yields 1 academic credit (e.g., 135 hours = 3 credits; maximum 6 credits allowed).
Internship Learning Agreement (Form INT-101) must be signed by employer and faculty advisor before work begins.
Retroactive academic credit for completed internships is strictly disallowed under accreditation policy.

sections.heading: 2. Career Fairs & Professional Clinics Schedule
lines: Fall STEM & Tech Career Fair: October 8, 2026 (Student Union Grand Ballroom, 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM).
All-Majors Spring Career Expo: February 18, 2027.
Drop-in 15-minute resume and LinkedIn critique clinics: Tuesdays & Thursdays 1:00 PM - 3:00 PM (Career Center).
Mock interview booking: Schedule 45-minute behavioral/technical sessions via horizon.joinhandshake.com.

sections.heading: 3. International Student Work Authorization (CPT & OPT)
lines: F-1 Visa holders must complete 1 full academic year of full-time enrollment before becoming eligible for CPT.
Curricular Practical Training (CPT) must be directly related to the student's major field of study.
CPT application deadline: Submit Form I-20-CPT to the International Student Office at least 15 days before start date.

sections.heading: 4. Career Center Contacts
lines: Career Development Center: Success Hall, 2nd Floor | career@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-8200
Handshake Portal Support: handshake-help@horizon.edu

title: Campus Parking, Shuttle, and Transport Rules
summary: Permit tier fees for commuter and resident students, electric vehicle charging station rules, free campus shuttle timetables and routes, and parking enforcement violation penalties.

sections.heading: 1. Parking Permit Tiers & Annual Fees
lines: Commuter Student Permit (Lots C1-C6): $220 per academic year ($125 per single semester).
Resident Student Permit (Lots R1-R4): $340 per academic year (restricted to assigned residence hall perimeter).
Evening Only Permit (Valid after 4:30 PM and weekends): $85 per semester.
Daily scratch-off visitor passes: $8.00 per day; purchase at automated kiosks located at North and South Gates.

sections.heading: 2. Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations
lines: Campus features 24 Level-2 ChargePoint stations across Parking Garages A and B.
Charging rate: $0.14 per kWh for the first 3 hours. $5.00/hour idle fee applies after vehicle reaches 100% charge.
Vehicles parked in EV bays without actively charging will be ticketed $60 for unauthorized bay obstruction.

sections.heading: 3. Campus Shuttle Routes & Timetable
lines: Blue Line (Campus Perimeter Loop): Runs every 10 minutes from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM, Monday through Friday.
Gold Line (Downtown & Metro Transit Hub): Runs every 20 minutes from 7:00 AM to 1:00 AM daily.
Night Owl Safety Escort Shuttle: On-demand dispatch from 11:00 PM to 4:00 AM via Horizon Ride Mobile App.
All campus shuttles are 100% free with active Horizon University Student ID card tap.

sections.heading: 4. Violation Penalties & Appeals
lines: Parking without valid permit: $45 fine. Parking in marked ADA handicap stall without placard: $250 fine.
Unpaid citations: 3 or more unpaid tickets lead to automatic wheel boot installation ($100 removal charge).
Citations may be appealed within 10 calendar days at parking.horizon.edu/appeals.

sections.heading: 5. Parking Office Contacts
lines: Parking Services: North Campus Garage Suite 100 | parking@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-7275 (PARK)
Dispatch & Roadside Lockout Help: (555) 019-7276

title: Student Clubs, Events, and Athletics Handbook
summary: Procedures for officially chartering a student organization, event grant funding allocations, student recreation and gym access policies, and intramural league registration.

sections.heading: 1. Chartering a Recognized Student Organization (RSO)
lines: Requirement: Minimum of 8 enrolled student founding members and 1 full-time faculty/staff advisor.
Must submit club constitution and bylaws to the Student Activities Council (SAC) by October 1 or February 1.
Mandatory leadership training: Club President and Treasurer must attend the Fall Risk & Finance Seminar.
Chartered RSOs receive free on-campus meeting room reservations and official club @horizon.edu email alias.

sections.heading: 2. Student Organization Activity Grants & Funding
lines: Tier 1 New RSO Startup Grant: $500 automatic startup allocation for newly chartered organizations.
Annual Budget Allocation: Up to $4,500 granted based on membership size and campus impact proposal.
Special Event Funding: Applications for events exceeding $1,000 must be submitted 30 days prior to event date.
Purchase reimbursements require itemized receipts submitted within 14 calendar days of expenditure.

sections.heading: 3. Campus Recreation & Fitness Center Access
lines: Apex Recreation Center: 85,000 sq ft facility featuring Olympic swimming pool, indoor track, and climbing wall.
Hours of operation: Monday-Thursday 6:00 AM - Midnight; Friday 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM; Weekends 8:00 AM - 9:00 PM.
Access is 100% free for enrolled students via Horizon Mobile ID bar-code scanner.
Guest passes: $10 per day (maximum 2 automated accompanied guests per enrolled student).

sections.heading: 4. Intramural Sports Leagues
lines: Fall leagues: 5v5 Basketball, Flag Football, Indoor Soccer, Co-ed Volleyball, Esports (Rocket League/Smash Bros).
Registration fee: $35 team entry fee for league play. Free agents can register at imleagues.com/horizon.
Championship winning teams receive official Horizon IM Championship t-shirts and trophy presentation.

sections.heading: 5. Student Life Contacts
lines: Office of Student Engagement: Campus Union Level 2, Suite 240 | studentlife@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-6100
Recreation Desk: recreation@horizon.edu | Phone: (555) 019-6150
